# TDPdf v1.21.0.0

A fork-sync release pulling the useful features and fixes from upstream [**SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF**](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF) (v1.7.2 and v1.7.3) and adapting them to TDPdf's diverged multi-tab architecture. This build ships everything merged to `main` since the last release, headlined by the changes below. See [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/doodlemania2/TDPdf/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the complete per-version history.

As always: this fork only exists because upstream KillerPDF is a genuinely great, dark-themed, no-telemetry, no-cloud Windows PDF editor. **Go star [the upstream project](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF).**

This one is headlined by a print dialog that can finally choose its paper, text selection that understands columns, and two memory fixes that matter a great deal on large documents. Porting also turned up three bugs in upstream's own versions of these changes, which are fixed here rather than inherited.

## Highlights

### The print dialog can finally choose its paper
Until now there was no way to pick a paper size or a tray — the print job carried only copies, orientation, color and duplex, so the stock was whatever the printer happened to default to. A Letter-default printer quietly printed A4 documents wrong, and there was nothing in the UI to say otherwise.

Both lists now come from the printer's own reported capabilities and rebuild when you switch printers. **Match document** and **Printer default** keep exactly today's behavior, so nothing changes unless you ask it to. Picking a size drives the preview and the actual job through the same path, so the sheet you see can't disagree with the paper it prints on.

The settings column is also organized into collapsible **PRINTER**, **LAYOUT** and **OUTPUT** sections — LAYOUT starts folded, since it holds the set-and-forget geometry — which is what keeps a narrow column usable while gaining two new controls.

### Text selection follows columns
Dragging down one column of a two-column PDF used to sweep the neighbouring column with it, and the copied text came out with the two columns interleaved line by line — unusable for anything academic or newspaper-shaped.

Selection now splits lines at column gutters and reads whole columns top to bottom, left to right, with titles and footers staying in place. Double-clicking to edit text picks up one run per column too, instead of a run whose text was both columns jammed together.

> Single-column pages and tables are explicitly left alone — see the fixes section, because getting that guarantee right is most of the work.

### Much lower memory on large documents
Two independent causes, both significant.

The re-sharpen pass in Continuous view was rendering pages at **twice** device resolution — four times the pixels and four times the bytes, for detail no display can actually resolve. And the page bitmap cache was limited only by page *count*, so 48 cached Letter pages could sit on roughly **630 MB in a single tab**, with every open tab keeping its own.

The re-sharpen pass now renders at the size it actually draws at, and the cache is budgeted in bytes as well as pages, keeping a moving window of nearby pages hot so scrolling still feels instant.

### Form fields stop showing double
Filled form fields were being painted twice — once baked into the page image, once by the live editable field on top — which showed up as a ghosted, slightly offset copy of your own text behind itself. That's gone.

Printing, flattening, exporting and thumbnails still include the filled values, because there the pixels *are* the output.

**Comb fields** are supported now too: the ones printed as a row of little boxes, one character per cell. Typing is capped at the cell count and each character is placed in its own cell when saved, the way Acrobat does it.

### Book layout for Two-Page view
Press **B** in Two-Page view and the cover displays alone, so facing pages pair the way a physical book falls open — 1, then 2‑3, then 4‑5 — instead of always pairing from the first page.

### Levels, for pale scans
Transform gains a **LEVELS** section: black point, white point and midtone gamma, for rescuing washed-out or faint scans. Unlike perspective correction it applies across a whole page selection, since it doesn't depend on any one page's geometry.

### Smaller things
- **The current page shows in a corner badge** that slides away when the view settles, replacing the page tooltip that used to trail the cursor.
- **Drop PDFs or images onto the Pages sidebar** to append them to the open document.
- **Click the status line** — or press **Shift+F4** — to see the open file's size, then get your previous status back.
- **Your last manual zoom is restored** when you reopen a document, instead of every open resetting to a fit.
- **The Outlines sidebar** opens with top-level bookmarks visible and deeper levels folded, and remembers what you expanded when you switch tabs.
- **Documents get keyboard focus on open**, so Space and arrow-scrolling inside a zoomed page work without clicking first.
- **Exported images carry the DPI you chose** in their metadata instead of always claiming 96, so a 300 DPI export places at its true physical size.

## Fixes worth calling out

- **Saved highlights washed out the text underneath.** They burned as a near-opaque rectangle painted over the words; they now darken the paper instead, so the text stays crisp — the way every other PDF viewer highlights.
- **Saving a rotated page could permanently clip it.** A page opened at 90° or 270° had its page box swapped on save, cutting off content for good.
- **Editing text lost the font whenever the PDF named it in PostScript form.** `ArialMT`, `TimesNewRomanPSMT` and `Helvetica` name no installed Windows font, so the editor silently substituted something else and the save fell back to the default — the bold/italic was right but the typeface was gone, which reads as "all my formatting disappeared".
- **The view didn't re-render when you moved the window to a monitor with a different scale factor.** At a manual zoom the page just sat there, upscaled from the old monitor's render.

### Three bugs in upstream's own changes, fixed here rather than inherited

- **Clicking in the right column put the caret in the left one.** Upstream's column work never updated the click-to-caret test, which takes the first line containing the point you clicked — and once columns exist, the left column always comes first. Every click in a right-hand column landed at the end of the left column's line.
- **Ordinary single-column pages got reordered.** Upstream groups columns unconditionally, so a letter with a right-aligned date, a centred title and a short salutation reads back as salutation, title, date. TDPdf requires real evidence of a gutter before believing in columns, plus a second check that keeps table rows row-major — a table row splits at its cell gaps exactly like a column gutter, and an invoice read column-major gives you every name, then every quantity, then every price. If either check fails, the page comes out exactly as it did before, so a misjudgement can never produce a worse order.
- **Windows fonts ending in "MT" stopped resolving.** Upstream's font-name cleanup turns `BellMT` into `Bell` and `Gill Sans MT` into `Gill Sans ` — trailing space included — which match no installed font. TDPdf already resolved those correctly, so adopting that change verbatim would have broken working documents.

## Notes

**Not ported:** the seven new themes, all localization (TDPdf is English-only), per-pane night mode and the split-pane fixes, machine-wide `killerpdf://` protocol registration, and the family file-dialog work — which includes v1.7.3's image preview pane, since it lives inside the custom file picker this fork declined in v1.20. Our image dialogs are the standard Windows ones, so there's nothing to attach a preview to without adopting the whole picker.

Upstream's book layout also re-anchors which page renders as the primary one. That isn't ported: in TDPdf the sidebar selection *is* the primary page, relied on throughout, and re-anchoring it would misplace annotations and break search highlighting. Paging is fully book-aware and the cover renders alone; jumping straight to a specific page still shows that page plus the next, which is what Two-Page has meant here since the feature was added.

**Verified rather than assumed:** horizontal touchpad and tilt-wheel scrolling was already implemented here back in v1.19.

**Needs Windows testing.** This release changes the render budgets, the save geometry, the print job, text selection and the form-field render path, none of which can be exercised on the macOS build machine. If you hit something, please [open an issue](https://github.com/doodlemania2/TDPdf/issues).
